title: Interactive Art Design - Tea Space
subtitle: Assisting postgraduate students as technical advisors in designing interactive devices and creating mechanical structures

mainContent.content: Technical advisor collaboration for a tea-space interactive installation. The design goal is quiet tactility: ritual, humidity, touch, and motion read as one unified atmosphere.

content.title: Bamboo cross structure suspended in darkness, casting a deliberate shadow with circular floor marker reading 'Do not climb'

mainContent.content: A cross-shaped bamboo installation hangs in darkness, its shadow becoming an interactive element. A floor marker invites careful engagement from visitors below.

content.title: Intricate paper-cut art installation with geometric models and shadow projections in the exhibition space

mainContent.content: Fine paper-cut art creates layered light and shadow, complementing mechanical elements with organic delicacy. Geometric models sit alongside the installation on display tables.
Technology serves the mood, not the other way around. Bamboo, paper, brass, and wood work together — the shadow cast by the cross structure becomes material itself.
